name: Kwer
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record kwer1265 (JSON) and OLAC 'resources in and about the Kwer language' (the Internet Archive 2026-06-09, index dated 2025-11-04)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog: only med is Wilbrink 2004 Appendices, a wordlist or less; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. OLAC : only the Glottolog and Ethnologue records, no archived recordings or descriptions.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco & Sebastian Fedden. 2014. Greater Awyu and Greater Ok: inheritance or contact? Oceanic Linguistics 53(1): 1-36 (HAL deposit hal-03950196)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level remark only, p. 2: 'While Mountain Ok languages are described as tonal (Telefol, Tifal, Mian), in Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages it is not the tone contour but lexical stress that seems to be distinctive.' 'Kwer' and 'Kopkaka' occur 0 times in the text layer; not a statement about Kwer and does not say where stress falls.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Kopkaka' and 'West Ok'. Newguineaworld (Santa Fe Institute; UZH mirror), DokuWiki raw export, downloaded 2026-09-17
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. Phonology section '[under construction]'; only 'Wilbrink (2004: 29-58) gives 12 consonants and 5 vowels for Kopkaka of Seradela'. Source inventory names Wilbrink 2004 (Kwer comparative terms pp. 109a-109f after Mark Donohue), Kroneman 2010 (unpublished Kopkaka grammar), Kroneman n.d. (Unokob vocabulary). No 'kwer' or 'burumakok' page exists in the West Ok namespace (saved as *).

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project entry 4461 'Kwer' (the Internet Archive 2025-08-10); SIL ISO 639-3 code record kwr; Badan Bahasa Peta Bahasa entry 'Kopkaka' (idb=495)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: ELP repeats Ethnologue 18 (100 speakers, 1998 M. Donohue) and Glottolog coordinates, bibliography tab empty. ISO record is code-only. Peta Bahasa : Kopkaka villages Seredela, Yebor, Mosomduba, Murwedala, Muruf, dialectometry only; Kwer not named; no phonology.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 18th ed., entry 'Kwer'. Dallas: SIL International. (Internet Archive copy 2016-12-01)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Population 100 (1998 M. Donohue). Location Papua Province, Jayawijaya regency, Kurima subdistrict, Kwer village.. Classification Trans-New Guinea, Ok-Awyu, Ok, Western. Dialects None known. Reportedly similar to Kopkaka [opk]; may be considered the same language.' No typology field. The 2025 Ethnologue page is a paywalled shell.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2012 Part I: 269-312
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Kopkaka appears only in a subject-suffix comparison table citing 'Kroneman 2010:11' (unpublished Kopkaka grammar sketch); 'Kwer' occurs 0 times.

sources.citation: Kroneman, Dick. 2010. Kopkaka grammar sketch. Unpublished manuscript (cited by de Vries, Wester & van den Heuvel 2012 and by Usher, Newguineaworld)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other description of the Kwer-Kopkaka language; a grammar sketch normally opens with a phonology section that would state stress placement. Unpublished; author affiliated with SIL/VU Amsterdam Una project.

sources.citation: Wilbrink, Ans. 2004. The Kopkaka of Papua. Provisional notes on their language, its language affiliation and on the Kopkaka culture. MA thesis, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, 219 pp. (phonology pp. 29-58; Kwer comparative wordlists pp. 109a-109f)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only phonology of the Kwer-Kopkaka group; Ethnologue says Kwer 'may be considered the same language' as Kopkaka, so any stress statement in its phonology chapter would be the best available proxy, and its Kwer wordlists (Yasid/Kwer, Kwer-Donohue) may carry stress marks. Glottolog (Hammarström) holds a private PDF; no public copy found (VU portal, WorldCat, Google Books, IA, HathiTrust).

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1998. Kwer survey wordlist(s), Kurima subdistrict (source of Ethnologue's population figure and of the 'Kwer-Donohue' list in Wilbrink 2004)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The primary Kwer field data; a phonetically transcribed survey wordlist could show stress marks even without a statement. Not deposited in OLAC/PARADISEC as far as the OLAC listing shows.

sources.citation: Kroneman, Dick. n.d. Survey vocabulary of Kopkaka of Unokob village (unpublished; digitized copy via Paul Whitehouse / SIL, cited by Usher)

sources.note: Further primary wordlist for the Kopkaka-Kwer language; may carry stress marks.

sources.citation: Wilbrink, Ans. 2004. Appendices. In: The Kopkaka of Papua. Provisional notes on their language, its language affiliation and on the Kopkaka culture, pp. 97-219. MA thesis, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. (Glottolog ref 310961; the only Glottolog reference for kwer1265)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: listed by Glottolog as an overview;comparative;wordlist, med_type a wordlist or less; language_note lists 'Yasid/Kwer = Kwer [kwr]' and 'Kwer-Donohue [kwr]' among ~20 comparative wordlists. Kwer figures only as wordlists (Usher: pp. 109a-109f 'Buramakok and Kwer villages after Mark Donohue'). No public copy; nothing on stress recorded.
